This is a fantastic game, on every front. If you're looking for a Darksouls-lite experience, either as a Soulslike newcomer or a veteran, this is a fantastic experience. I played on Veteran and I only really struggled on a handful of bosses, but my losses never felt unfair or buggy. The diversity of classes and flexibility to hotswap classes is easily my favorite part of the game, and the amount of flavor involved in such checks are really fun!

I do have one serious critique, however. REMOVE THE 65 TRAIT POINT CAP!!!! it has NO business being there! One of the things I love to do in every Darksouls games is hyper-level my character into oblivion and be an unstoppable badass, but I can't do that here, and that's disappointing.

Also, some PvP support could be fun, but I never cared for it even in Darksouls.

Honestly never expected a sequel so soon, to top it off with a massive improvement, but it is definitely a very welcome one. Simply put this is a randomly generated dungeon crawler with a sprinkle of the souls like genre and also third person shooter. This game is pretty much an RPG with the new systems and has a ton of content to explore and secrets to discover (some might be a little ridiculous to figure out on your own) and overall, as what was first stated, an impressive successor to Remnant: From the ashes. The archetype system complimented with uniqueness to every archetype but at the same time not too different to be completely out of chemistry, the balancing on most aspect of the game, the impressive art direction and visuals that almost makes it a completely different game compared to the first game, even the music itself also is much more memorable and cinematic to the experience. If there is anything to complain about for this game, it is the performance issues that are heavily reliant on upscaling, to which they have addressed and hopefully will be fixed soon, and also the offensive builds variety being completely overshadowed by crit stacking. While it is true remnant 1 did have crit as something powerful too, we still had more options for offensive options such as slayer weakspot focused build, DoTs builds, and mod spam builds weren't reliant on crit to be viable either. Either way however they want to address this by either nerfing crit, buffing everything else, or giving more options, i don't really mind since crit is so easily to be ingrained to your build that at this point it's become one of the core traits lol. 

Tldr; Impeccable sequel with minor flaws, i would highly recommend you give this a try even if you are not a fan of the souls like genre, also be a little patient with performance problems that could occur occassionally, and lastly playing in co-op is definitely the best experience, but doesn't mean the singleplayer experience is boring in the slightest or overwhelmingly difficult

Note: Review edited, go to bottom.
Pros:
-Many hours of gameplay. The game features Elden Ring like open world and zones, however each zone is randomized per playthrough per player.
-Most of the items in the game are hidden, forcing you to explore and hunt for secrets if you want to use any cool weapons or armor. Great for players that like scavenger hunts.
-It's not extremely difficult like Dark Souls but also not too easy. I'd say it's the perfect balance.
-Graphically it looks great and the audio is decent also, although the soundtrack is not very memorable.
-Features many classes and weapon types, allowing each player to build for a specific scenario or team composition.
-Drop-in Co-op. With Friends or Randoms. 4 players Max.

Cons:
-Runs like a trash compactor on fire. My RTX 3060 Ti is constantly on fire, there seems to be no optimization for this game's assets whatsoever. Changing the graphics settings has little to no impact.
-Many... Many... Many bugs. I'm not kidding. If you're playing the campaign and only doing the main story, you might only encounter 1 or 2 bugs. IF like me you choose to explore the many secrets and collect all the equipment in the game, you will encounter dozens. I'm not talking minor bugs either... I'm talking bugs that will force you to Die or even RESET YOUR ENTIRE CAMPAIGN/ADVENTURE. Wasting hours of your time. Some have been fixed by the devs. Many remain.
-Clutter. The game has a lot of items such as: weapons, armor, rings, amulets and the good ol Dark Souls flask aka Relic. However a LOT of these, and I do mean a lot of these, are completely useless in terms of performance or pretty much equivalent to each other. The only Unique or remotely Useful items you will find are hidden away in the farthest corners of the map behind some very cryptic secrets that will 100% require a guide. Everything else you will find in your campaign is mediocre.
It also doesn't help that RNG plays the biggest role in this. Many items and Quests are locked behind RNG. Meaning if you don't have them in your world, you need to Reset and try again. Over... and Over...

Summary:
This game is fun, I'm not gonna lie. If you're looking for a game and you plan on just rushing the campaign without bothering with any of the side quests... Go for it. Buy it and enjoy.
But if you're like me and you want to experience this game in it's entirety... I'd say wait for bug fixes or a Sale and get it cheaper.
I've literally wasted tens of hours of frustration trying to bypass bugs or get good RNG. To the point where Fun turned into Chore.

------

Edit: The devs have been very active in fixing many bugs, their patch notes are literally too long for 1 post. Considering the dedication of the devs and how much the game has improved since release, Many of the softlock bugs have been fixed by now.

But be warned there are still Many... MANY bugs. If you're a completionist like me and want to get 100% in this game you WILL pull your hair out due to the amount of dumb bugs that will soflock and block you from doing so.

If you're still unconvinced of just how much of a buggy mess this game is, look at the discussion forums or look on reddit. Out of all my hours spent playing this game, at least half of them were me punching a wall in my room out of frustration.

I will NOT recommend this game at full price. Wait for a 50% discount. Developers need to learn to Release FULL games if they want FULL price. Half-assed games deserve Half-price.

------

Edit2: There have been a lot of Bug fixes and QoL updates. The game is currently playable without encountering too many bugs so I could recommend it at maybe a 20% discount. However a lot of the root issues still exist.

Very fun, challenging, beautiful game. I would never have bought this if I hadn't gotten to try the first one for free. I am really glad I did though. As someone who tends to not like Souls-like, I really love both Remnant games. They are challenging but not punishing to the point of making you feel like it's impossible. Remnant is just hard enough to make things interesting, and you will die over and over but if you keep trying then you can definitely progress in the game. Maybe this has changed my mind on these type of games and I will actually go back and try more Souls-like. I thoroughly enjoyed losing and losing again (and again) but finally succeeding and getting to experience the satisfaction that comes along with the determination that it took not to give up.

The game is beautiful, it looks AMAZING on my 38" ultrawide, Unreal Engine 5 (and its Nanite feature) makes everything so amazingly detailed in this game. I highly recommend it, either for solo or Co-op. You can really have a blast if you play this with a friend, or even strangers too I suppose. Getting some backup can really be the difference in winning that boss fight or not.

The performance/optimization on PC is still a little rough, though. There are some spots in the game where my system will run the game at over 90fps on high at 3840x1600 using FSR balanced, but then there are other sections where I can't even maintain 50 fps when turning everything down to low. I think the game is CPU limited, but even my 5800x3d can't overcome theses issues. It is somewhat playable on the Steam Deck, just be prepared for 20-30fps and needing to use FSR/XeSS Performance level for upscaling. I honestly recommend XeSS on non-Nvidia GPUs. Image Quality is quite a bit better than FSR 2.
